A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMT research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, training-cost measurements, and initialization ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds MS-COCO text-to-image experiments in Section 4.2 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The three-stage CMT pipeline, trajectory-based regression targets, and CM/MF objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure; the MS-COCO experiment applies it with another backbone and training configuration.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual training and evaluation on MS-COCO text-to-image generation at 256×256. This substantially extends coverage from unconditional and class-conditioned generation to text-conditioned generation, while retaining all original datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. KD and Slow CMT already appeared in v1 Appendix C.2. The new MS-COCO comparison extends the existing random-initialized MF, SiT-initialized MF, and CMT comparison design to another task.

E3.justification: The added MS-COCO experiment introduces a task-specific protocol: validation-set FID, an MM-DiT backbone, REPA training, a SiT teacher trained for 50k iterations, CFG scale 2, and eight-step Heun trajectories for mid-training. Existing benchmark settings and ablation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Footnote 1 in v2 newly reports that data-dependent terminal samples and data-free prior samples perform identically, without numerical details. The mid-training-duration and KD/Slow CMT ablations retain their settings and findings when moved from v1 Appendix C to v2 Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The informal observation about restarting SiT-initialized MF with another seed is retained; the new experiments add no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds a complete quality-and-cost comparison for text-to-image generation. Table 5 reports one/two-step FIDs of 15.97/5.42 for random-initialized MF, 15.55/5.26 for SiT-initialized MF, and 15.12/5.01 for CMT, with total training times of 60, 60, and 32 hours respectively. The SiT teacher's 50-step FID is 4.73. These are new task results; matched pre-existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C.2 adds an explicit complexity comparison with Slow CMT: O(1) amortized teacher evaluations per pair for CMT versus O(NFEs_traj), implying approximately M-fold teacher-evaluation overhead for Slow CMT. The existing flow-map derivations, assumptions, theorems, and Appendix F proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction adds the specific claim that CMT achieves the best MS-COCO FID among the evaluated configurations with approximately 47% less total training time. The central mid-training contribution, abstract, conclusion, and original benchmark claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 suggests that high one-step MS-COCO FIDs may reflect dataset limitations, an interpretation not established by a dedicated analysis. It also expands the explanation of trajectory reuse and explicitly acknowledges that the Slow CMT comparison lacks an exhaustive sweep matching GPU hours.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 supplies explicit sampling, teacher-freezing, initialization, and update steps. Appendix B.6 documents the new MS-COCO training settings, including guidance parameters and the 112-pair mid-training batch. v2 also specifies default log-SNR solver schedules; existing benchmark details and code/model access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for U-ViT, MM-DiT, MS-COCO, REPA, sampling-schedule optimization, and Lai et al.'s diffusion-model principles. These provide additional context for the new experiment and solver discussion without substantially redefining CMT's relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial structural reorganization: related work moves into Section 2.3, existing ablations move into Section 4.3, and Appendices A–E are reorganized around model relationships, implementation, costs, losses, and samples. The main theoretical exposition is condensed, and algorithm, reproducibility, ethics, and language-model-use sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds the MS-COCO results table and a full-page algorithm display, with accompanying table placement, caption, and spacing adjustments. Existing figures retain their plotted findings and image content, and the original numerical tables retain their structures apart from minor labeling and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The MS-COCO experiment provides useful additional evidence for CMT's applicability to text-conditioned generation. Algorithm 1, more accessible ablations, and the expanded cost discussion improve clarity and assessability. These are bounded gains: the principal results and proofs remain unchanged, the new terminal-distribution comparison lacks quantitative detail, and the proposed dataset explanation for high one-step FID remains speculative.
